steps.title: Relate heat to temperature rise
steps.narration: A larger mass or a larger specific heat needs more energy for the same rise in temperature.

steps.title: Convert the mass
steps.narration: Convert grams to kilograms because the given specific heat is measured per kilogram.

steps.title: Find the temperature rise
steps.narration: Divide the heat supplied by the heat needed for a rise of one degree. A change of one kelvin equals a change of one Celsius degree. Choose C.

steps.title: Use similar triangles
steps.narration: The straight ray through the pinhole makes the same angle on both sides, so height divided by distance is the same for both triangles.

steps.title: Compare the image measurements
steps.narration: The image height and distance are both in centimetres, so their units cancel. This gives the scale of the triangle.

steps.title: Find the building's height
steps.narration: The building's height is half its distance from the pinhole. That gives one hundred and fifty metres. Choose D.

steps.title: Find the image height
steps.narration: A plane mirror gives an upright image the same size as the object, so the image height is also two centimetres.

steps.title: Write the size ratio
steps.narration: Linear magnification compares image height with object height. The units cancel because both heights are measured in centimetres.

steps.title: Calculate magnification
steps.narration: The two heights are equal, so the magnification is one point zero. Choose B.

steps.title: Use the perpendicular speed
steps.narration: Only motion across the field lines produces the voltage. The sine gives the component of velocity across the field.

steps.title: Evaluate the sine
steps.narration: At thirty degrees the perpendicular component is half the given speed.

steps.title: Find the induced voltage
steps.narration: Multiply field strength, length and perpendicular speed to get thirty-seven point five volts. Choose A.

steps.title: Set up repeated halving
steps.narration: Raise one half to the number of half-lives because each interval halves whatever remains at that time.

steps.title: Count the halvings
steps.narration: It takes three halvings to reach one hundred and twenty-five atoms.

steps.title: Find the elapsed time
steps.narration: Each of the three intervals lasts twenty seconds, so sixty seconds have passed. Choose C.

steps.title: Connect period and length
steps.narration: The period grows with the square root of length. We can compare periods without knowing the numerical value of gravity.

steps.title: Take the period ratio
steps.narration: The common factor involving gravity and two pi cancels when we divide the periods.

steps.title: Find the scale factor
steps.narration: The new length is double, so the new period is the old period times the square root of two.

steps.title: Find the new period
steps.narration: Multiply the original two seconds by the square root of two. Choose C.

steps.title: Use constant acceleration
steps.narration: Uniform deceleration means the velocity changes by the same amount every second.

steps.title: Substitute the speeds
steps.narration: The train loses two metres per second of speed each second until its speed reaches zero.

steps.title: Find the stopping time
steps.narration: Divide the total speed lost by the amount lost each second. The train takes ten seconds. Choose B.

steps.title: Find the velocity ratio
steps.narration: Both ends turn through the same angle, so the longer arm moves twice as far as the shorter arm.

steps.title: Find mechanical advantage
steps.narration: Mechanical advantage is the actual force gain. Efficiency makes it smaller than the ideal velocity ratio.

steps.title: Relate load and effort
steps.narration: Mechanical advantage compares the load lifted with the effort applied, so the effort is the load divided by that gain.

steps.title: Calculate the effort
steps.narration: Divide one hundred and eighty newtons by one point eight to get one hundred newtons. Choose C.

steps.title: Set up the proportion
steps.narration: The fraction of the length above the ice mark equals the fraction of the temperature range above zero degrees.

steps.title: Simplify the fraction
steps.narration: Twenty degrees is one fifth of the full Celsius range between these two marks.

steps.title: Find the distance
steps.narration: One fifth of four hundred millimetres is eighty millimetres above the ice mark. Choose D.
